newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzania pins investment hopes on gold mining.
newsitem.headline: Tanzania pins investment hopes on gold mining.

text.p: Gold prospecting in Tanzania has added additional sparkle to hopes of a mining-led economic recovery in one of the globe's poorest nations, government and industry officials said on Friday.

"There's certainly an exploration boom going on. The key factor on how this will translate into the opening of new mines will be the implementation of recent government policies," said Tony Macfarlane, General Manager of East Africa Mines Ltd.
East Africa Mines is a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Canadian-based East Africa Gold Corporation.

On Wednesday, Energy and Mines Minister Abdallah Kigoda signed a $50 million joint venture deal with Australian gold miner Resolute Samantha Ltd and its British partner Samax Resources. The contract covers a 14-month mine development programme with production scheduled for mid-1998.

Macfarlane told Reuters Tanzania's gold mining industry had huge potential and could kick-start an economic recovery. Tanzania had a rich minerals resource base and economic and political policies were becoming friendly to the industry, he added.

Figures provided by the Tanzanian Chamber of Mines show that between 1992 and 1995 the government approved only 85 prospecting licenses, mostly for gold mining companies. But in 1996, a total of 283 licenses were given. About $80 million was projected to be spent on gold exploration in 1997.
The gold boom had sparked a surge in support facilities essential for long-term growth of a mining industry.

In other developments, the government is currently drafting a new mining act which would address critical issues affecting the mining industry, including security of tenure, taxation and environmental regulations.
There are now 15 mining and exploration firms active in Tanzania.

"I think mining is the future of this country. Every year we will be giving to this government $66 million in revenue from July 1999 onwards," said Bill Bali, resident director of Kahama Mining Corporation Ltd.

Kahama is a subsidiary of Canadian-based Sutton Resources -- currently developing a world class gold project at northern Bulyankulu worth $150 million. The Tanzanian government owns a 15 percent equity in the company.
